Independent symbolic check of the support-labeled triangle constraints and tail calculation
correctness.rationale: Homogeneity and one-point extension identify types over the named vertices with positive distance vectors. The only invalid pairings are 1/3 on edges and 1/1 at capped distance 3. For the distance-one support S, this requires diameter at most two and fixes all its external neighbors to 2; outside its closed neighborhood each label is freely 2 or 3. Singletons and edge pairs yield the vertex and edge terms. Every remaining nonempty support contains a distance-two pair and is assigned to its unique tree midpoint c; it consists of at least two neighbors A of c, with c optional. The closed-neighborhood sizes are 1+sum(deg(v):v in A) without c and 1+deg(c)+sum(deg(v)−1:v in A) with it, since branches do not meet away from c. Expanding the subset products gives the stated normalized identity. A one-leaf extension on a tail with the two internal degrees 2 changes the normalized vertex, edge and centered contributions by 1/8, 1/16 and 1/16, respectively. The bases are N(P4)=37, N(E7)=384 and N(E8)=840, so adding 1/4 to the normalized count per extension proves both formulas and the gap at every n>=8. Independent raw triangle testing of every labeled Prüfer tree through order seven matched both counting formulas; minima were (3,7,17,37,82,180,384) with labeled multiplicities (1,1,3,12,60,360,840). Each minimizing shape is a path through six and is E7 at seven; P7 has 392 types.
residual_risks: The finite census stops at seven. The family E_n for n>=8 defeats the path but is not shown to minimize among all trees. The result does not treat the all-nonedges-distance-two graph metric.

value.rationale: Counting logical one-point extensions is a natural metric-space invariant. The neighborhood formula turns a priori nonlocal triangle conditions into a local tree calculation, and a sharply determined seven-vertex counterexample rules out path minimality in a different setting from graph homomorphisms. The explicit gap at every greater order makes the failure structural rather than an isolated anomaly.
residual_risks: The proof does not identify the global minimizer at larger orders or generalize to arbitrary finite metric bases.
